name: Hock E. Tan

career.title: Senior Vice President, then Chief Executive Officer (from 1999)

background_rationale: Though trained as a mechanical engineer, he built his career in corporate finance and general management at PepsiCo, GM, Commodore and Integrated Circuit Systems before using acquisitions to build Avago into Broadcom.

notable.summary: Broadcom's roughly $117 billion bid for Qualcomm, launched under Tan in November 2017, was blocked by a U.S. presidential order citing national security concerns.
Broadcom agreed to acquire cloud software company VMware for about $61 billion; the deal closed in November 2023.
Broadcom and OpenAI announced a collaboration to deploy 10 gigawatts of custom AI accelerators, starting in the second half of 2026 and finishing by the end of 2029.
European cloud trade group CISPE filed an antitrust complaint with the European Commission over Broadcom's VMware licensing changes, which Broadcom disputes.

personal_story.hook: A Penang teenager whose parents couldn't afford college, Hock Tan reached MIT on a scholarship.
personal_story.summary: Tan was born in Penang, Malaysia, around 1951-52. In 1971, at 18, he left for MIT on a scholarship, later saying his parents could not have afforded to send him to college. He earned bachelor's and master's degrees in mechanical engineering in 1975 and then an MBA from Harvard. He worked in finance at PepsiCo, General Motors and Commodore and ran Hume Industries in Malaysia, then became CEO of Integrated Circuit Systems in 1999. In 2006 he took over Avago Technologies, newly spun out of Agilent, and used a string of acquisitions to turn it into today's Broadcom.

facts.label: Family background
facts.value: Says his parents could not have afforded to send him to college

facts.label: Turning point
facts.value: 1971: left Malaysia for MIT on a scholarship at age 18

facts.label: Mentor
facts.value: Called MIT professor Nam P. Suh 'an inspiration' and funded a professorship in his honor

quote.text: My parents could not have afforded to send me to college, much less MIT, but this great American educational institution took a chance on me, sight unseen, by giving me a scholarship
quote.context: Remarks at the White House Oval Office, Nov. 2017, announcing Broadcom's move of its headquarters to the U.S.
